about: The registry of FEATURE shorts (make_feature_story.py; SKILL.md, section Feature shorts). One entry = one feature of the site, the one question it answers and the real card that answers it. Schema /2 (owner verdict 2026-11-10: "they arent good, only the last one show the visuals correctly as it shown on website"): the payoff is the site's card WHOLE, captured as one strip of the page at phone width (`site`), shown large in one window, scrolled like a thumb when it is taller than the stage, with the key outlined where it stands. The card is chosen by its VISUAL: one of its parts is a drawn chart (`site.charts`, default the part named chart), and the page stands only where the window's edges cut no row. Fragment cards, crops and 6x key captures are refused by the registry, the capture gate and the story gate; the gates still trust the box an entry NAMES as its card, so a new entry is looked at by a person (SKILL.md, Adding a feature). Lines never hold a number, a ticker, a name, a weekday or a period: those are {slots}, read from the capture's text on the render day. Every capitalised word a line types, the first word of a sentence included, is listed in proper_words (a person or a company is never typed). `hold` on an entry: rendered for review, not posted, and why.

features.title: Congress trades (market in pictures)
features.post_note: The card counts the stock trades members of Congress DISCLOSED in the last 30 days (the site's own definition: backend/src/slices/market_flows WINDOW_DAYS, checked 2026-11-10; the card itself shows no dates). Say "disclosed in the last 30 days" in the post text. Counts, not dollars. The card's "Most traded" row shows tickers with their small company logos, as the site draws it; a ticker whose logo the site has not got stands there as text.
features.about_page: /market is a permanent redirect to the home page's Market section (/#market): the capture asks for /market and the browser ends on /#market. The card is far below the page header, so the header is not in the strip (the brand pill carries the brand). The page stands on the card's top (title, headline and the whole chart of sectors), scrolls to the Most traded row and the card's end, and comes back for the outline.
refuse_if: No stock trades by members of Congress were disclosed

checks.why: the story is a day the card shows more sells than buys

features.hold: OPEN OWNER DECISION (2026-11-10): the card shows other companies' ticker logos as the site draws them. Rendered for review only: do not post until the owner rules. If he rules them out, drop this feature (masking the card breaks payoff rule 1).

features.title: Insider trades (market in pictures)
features.post_note: Open-market buys and sales by company officers and directors of their own company's stock; the card says 30-day totals: say "in the last 30 days" in the post text (the hook alone reads as one event). The rows show tickers with their small company logos, as the site draws it. LOOK AT screens/logos.png: on 2026-11-10 the site drew another firm's logo beside one ticker (reported to Infra as a site bug); a capture with a wrong or missing logo is not shipped.
features.about_page: /market is a permanent redirect to the home page's Market section (/#market). The card is far below the page header, so the header is not in the strip. The card holds two charts, one under the other: the page stands on the BOUGHT list while the first line is read, scrolls to the SOLD list and stands there while the second line is read (site.read_end), then comes back and the sold figure is outlined in the headline.

checks.why: the story is a day the card shows more sold than bought

features.hold: OPEN OWNER DECISION (2026-11-10): the card shows other companies' ticker logos as the site draws them. Rendered for review only: do not post until the owner rules. If he rules them out, drop this feature (masking the card breaks payoff rule 1).

features.title: Portfolio concentration (sample portfolio)
features.post_note: The numbers are the site's read-only sample portfolio: the video says "your money" and never shows the READ-ONLY SAMPLE label, so the post text MUST say it is the sample portfolio. Same page and the same donut as the portfolio short: do not post the two close together.
features.about_page: The strip is the head of the Portfolio Concentration card: from its title to its two-ring donut, with the air the site leaves under the chart (the card's box for the gates ends at the donut: the SECTORS, industry and holdings lists below it belong to the portfolio short). It is shown whole in one frame, without a scroll. The card starts a screen below the page header, so the header is not in the strip.

values.rx: (?P<share>\d+(?:\.\d+)?%) of your money is in (?P<n>\d+) chip companies\.

checks.why: the story is about a portfolio the page calls Concentrated
the hook needs several chip companies
the hook says the chip companies are a few of many holdings

features.title: Portfolio page (sample portfolio)
features.post_note: The numbers are the site's read-only sample portfolio (the screen says READ-ONLY SAMPLE for the first second): say so in the post text. Same page and the same donut as the concentration short: do not post the two close together.
features.about_page: The strip is the page from its header down to the second row of the SECTORS list. One slow thumb scroll from the page's top (our header, READ-ONLY SAMPLE, the value) through the card's title and headline to where the whole two-ring donut stands above the SECTORS heading and its first row; the page stays there and that row, the largest sector, is outlined in place. The card's box for the gates ends at that row.

values.rx: (?P<sector>[A-Z][A-Za-z &]+) is (?P<pct>\d+(?:\.\d+)?%) of your money\. In the S&P 500 it's (?P<bench>\d+(?:\.\d+)?%)\.

checks.why: the story is about one sector holding a large share of the money
